# SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion

**ID:** `RUNBOOK-SEC-004`  
**Domain:** Security & Identity  
**Applies To:** Caddy Reverse Proxy, SSH Bastions, Super Admin Authentication Endpoints  
**Severity:** High to Critical

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
metadata.section: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
text:
## 1. Symptom Profile
- Surging volume of HTTP 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden responses on `/api/v1/auth/login`.
- High rate of repeated failed login attempts against identical or rotating usernames from specific external IP addresses.
- Security event detections: `brute_force_detected`, `ssh_auth_failure`, or `credential_stuffing_wave`.
- Elevated network connection states in `SYN_RECV` or rapid TCP connection recycling.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
text:
## 2. Root Cause Classification
- **Automated Credential Stuffing:** Botnet attacking exposed management endpoints with leaked credential lists.
- **Password Spray Attack:** Slow-rate attempts testing common passwords across hundreds of known enterprise usernames to avoid naive rate limits.
- **Port / Vulnerability Scanner:** Automated internet scanners (e.g., Shodan, Censys) probing for open admin dashboards or SSH ports.
- **Misconfigured Automation Script:** Internal agent or cron worker attempting to authenticate with an expired or rotated API key.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
text:
## 3. Immediate Diagnostic Commands
```bash

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
section: Identify top IP addresses generating failed login attempts
text:
# Identify top IP addresses generating failed login attempts
grep "401" /var/log/caddy/access.log | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 10

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
metadata.section: Identify top IP addresses generating failed login attempts

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
section: Inspect active TCP connections by remote address
text:
# Inspect active TCP connections by remote address
netstat -ntu | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -n

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
metadata.section: Inspect active TCP connections by remote address

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
section: Query CloudOps Intel Security Event audit log

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
metadata.section: Query CloudOps Intel Security Event audit log

title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion
text:
## 4. Remediation Steps
1. **Immediate IP Perimeter Block:**
   - Drop offending source IPs at firewall or Caddy level:
     `iptables -A INPUT -s <OFFENDING_IP> -j DROP` or add IP ban rule in Caddyfile reverse proxy block.
2. **Account Lockout & Password Invalidation:**
   - Temporarily suspend accounts targeted with > 10 failed attempts and require password reset via email verification.
3. **Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA):**
   - Ensure all admin and operator accounts require TOTP or security keys for privileged access.
4. **Audit Token Revocation:**
   - Invalidate active JWT refresh tokens if compromised credentials or session hijacking is suspected.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Brute Force Authentication & Perimeter Intrusion

# SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing

**ID:** `RUNBOOK-COST-006`  
**Domain:** Cloud FinOps & Cost Optimization  
**Applies To:** AWS EC2, GCP Compute Engine, Azure VMs, Idle Staging Hosts  
**Severity:** Medium

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
metadata.section: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing

title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
text:
## 1. Symptom Profile
- Unexpected spike in daily or monthly projected infrastructure spend (> 20% over 30-day baseline).
- Cost recommendation engine flags instances with sustained low utilization (< 10% CPU and memory) over 7+ days.
- Orphaned cloud assets: Unattached EBS/persistent volumes, unassociated Elastic IPs, or idle load balancers.
- Staging and development environments running 24/7 over non-business hours and weekends.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing

title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
text:
## 2. Root Cause Classification
- **Over-Provisioned Instance SKU:** Workload running on larger instance size (e.g. `c5.4xlarge`) than required by actual CPU/RAM peaks.
- **Abandoned Test Bench / Proof-of-Concept:** Temporary benchmarking instances left running indefinitely after project completion.
- **Continuous Runaway Auto-Scaling:** Faulty scale-down policy preventing replica reduction after traffic peak passes.
- **Unattached Storage Volumes:** Storage volumes retained after instance termination without retention justification.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing

title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
text:
## 3. Immediate Diagnostic Commands
```bash

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing

title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
section: Query active CloudOps Intel Cost Optimization recommendations
text:
# Query active CloudOps Intel Cost Optimization recommendations
SELECT host_id, recommendation_type, current_cost_usd, recommended_cost_usd, estimated_monthly_savings_usd 
FROM cost_recommendations 
WHERE status = 'open' 
ORDER BY estimated_monthly_savings_usd DESC;

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
metadata.section: Query active CloudOps Intel Cost Optimization recommendations

title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
section: Identify candidate instances with average CPU < 10% over last 7 days
text:
# Identify candidate instances with average CPU < 10% over last 7 days
SELECT host_id, AVG(cpu_percent) as avg_cpu 
FROM metrics 
WHERE timestamp >= datetime('now', '-7 days') 
GROUP BY host_id 
HAVING avg_cpu < 10.0;
```

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
metadata.section: Identify candidate instances with average CPU < 10% over last 7 days

title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing
text:
## 4. Remediation Steps
1. **Downsize Over-Provisioned Compute:**
   - Review workload peak usage and resize instances (e.g., migrate from `t3.large` to `t3.medium`).
2. **Schedule Automated Off-Hours Shutdown:**
   - Configure cron/lambda schedules to stop development and staging instances outside business hours (08:00–18:00 Mon–Fri) to save ~65% monthly run rate.
3. **Purge Orphaned Storage Volumes:**
   - Snapshot and delete unattached volumes older than 14 days.
4. **Implement AWS/GCP Budget Alerts:**
   - Establish automated spending threshold alerts at 80%, 100%, and 120% of monthly budget forecast.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Cloud Cost Anomalies & Idle Resource Rightsizing

# SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

**ID:** `RUNBOOK-DISK-003`  
**Domain:** Storage & Database Reliability  
**Applies To:** SQLite Databases, Log Partitions, System Root Drives  
**Severity:** Critical

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
metadata.section: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
text:
## 1. Symptom Profile
- Available disk space on partition drops below 10% or triggers `disk_percent > 90%` alert.
- Database write operations fail with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full` or `I/O error`.
- SQLite Write-Ahead Log (`cloud_intelligence.db-wal`) grows into hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes without checkpointing.
- Log rotation failures causing `/var/log` or application log directory bloating.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
text:
## 2. Root Cause Classification
- **Uncheckpointed WAL File:** Long-running read transactions holding open database locks, preventing SQLite WAL autocheckpoint.
- **Runaway Log Files:** Verbose `DEBUG` logging active in production without log rotation / retention limits.
- **Orphaned Temporary / Export Files:** Uncleaned scratch files, failed bulk import artifacts, or temporary crash dumps.
- **Log Archival Failure:** Backups or log shippers stalling and causing local queues to back up onto primary volumes.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
text:
## 3. Immediate Diagnostic Commands
```bash

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
section: Check filesystem free space and inode exhaustion
text:
# Check filesystem free space and inode exhaustion
df -h
df -i

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
metadata.section: Check filesystem free space and inode exhaustion

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
section: Find top 10 largest directories in application path
text:
# Find top 10 largest directories in application path
du -ah /path/to/app | sort -rh | head -n 10

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
metadata.section: Find top 10 largest directories in application path

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
text:
# On Windows PowerShell:
Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Select-Object Name, Used, Free, @{Name="PercentFree";Expression={[math]::Round($_.Free/($_.Used+$_.Free)*100,2)}}
Get-ChildItem -Path C:\CLoudProject -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 -Property FullName, Length
```

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation
text:
## 4. Remediation Steps
1. **Force SQLite WAL Checkpoint:**
   - Execute an explicit passive or truncate checkpoint against the database:
     `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);`
2. **Purge Rotated & Expired Logs:**
   - Compress or remove `.log.1`, `.log.2`, or logs older than retention policy (e.g., > 14 days).
3. **Verify Open Database File Handles:**
   - Ensure background tasks and connection pools close cursor transactions promptly.
4. **Provision Emergency Volume Expansion:**
   - If disk growth is legitimate due to telemetry ingestion rates, expand disk volume or configure metric downsampling.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Storage Exhaustion & Database WAL Log Accumulation

section: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
text:
# SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

**ID:** `RUNBOOK-CPU-001`  
**Domain:** Performance & Capacity  
**Applies To:** Linux/Windows Hosts, API Gateways, Microservices, Lab PCs  
**Severity:** High to Critical

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
metadata.section: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
text:
## 1. Symptom Profile
- Host CPU utilization sustained above 85% for more than 5 minutes.
- Elevated system load average exceeding the number of physical CPU cores.
- Thread starvation causing request timeouts, HTTP 504 Gateway Timeouts, or sluggish agent telemetry check-ins.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
text:
## 2. Root Cause Classification
- **Thread Loop / Uncontrolled Recursion:** Application bug executing tight spin-locks or unoptimized nested iterations.
- **Garbage Collection / JIT Thrashing:** High memory churn triggering perpetual stop-the-world or heavy background GC.
- **Crypto-Mining / Rogue Worker Process:** Unauthorized execution or orphaned background jobs consuming 100% of single/multi cores.
- **Sudden Traffic Spike:** Legitimate surge in inbound API requests without horizontal autoscaling triggers.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
text:
## 3. Immediate Diagnostic Commands
```bash

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
section: Identify top 5 CPU-consuming processes on Linux
text:
# Identify top 5 CPU-consuming processes on Linux
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -n 6

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
metadata.section: Identify top 5 CPU-consuming processes on Linux

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
section: Check per-core CPU utilization breakdown (user, system, iowait)
text:
# Check per-core CPU utilization breakdown (user, system, iowait)
mpstat -P ALL 1 3

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
metadata.section: Check per-core CPU utilization breakdown (user, system, iowait)

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
text:
# On Windows PowerShell:
Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 -Property Id, ProcessName, CPU, WorkingSet
```

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation
text:
## 4. Remediation Steps
1. **Targeted Process Intervention:**
   - If a rogue or non-critical process is identified, gracefully signal or terminate:
     `kill -15 <PID>` (or `Stop-Process -Id <PID> -Force` on Windows).
2. **Workload Throttle / Rate Limiting:**
   - Activate API rate limits or shed load at the Caddy proxy level using header rate limiting.
3. **Horizontal or Vertical Autoscaling:**
   - Provision additional worker replicas or upgrade the instance type if steady-state demand exceeds capacity.
4. **Agent Telemetry Verification:**
   - Confirm agent CPU returns to baseline below 65% in the CloudOps Intel Telemetry stream.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: High CPU Saturation & Process Starvation

# SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline

**ID:** `RUNBOOK-LAB-005`  
**Domain:** IoT & Lab Device Management  
**Applies To:** Computer Labs, Edge PCs, Local Hardware Agents, Monitoring Daemons  
**Severity:** Medium to High

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
metadata.section: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
text:
## 1. Symptom Profile
- Lab PC status transitions to `offline` or `unreachable` in the Device Management dashboard.
- Last heartbeat timestamp exceeds tolerance threshold (> 5 minutes without check-in).
- Local sensor metrics (temperature, fan speed, GPU state, power draw) cease updating.
- Room or rack-level environmental telemetry displays gaps or missing telemetry points.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
text:
## 2. Root Cause Classification
- **Host Sleep / Power State Transition:** Windows or Linux machine entering unexpected S3 Sleep, Hibernation, or Fast Startup shutdown.
- **Local Network Disconnection:** Physical Ethernet cable unplugged, switch port flapping, or local DHCP lease renewal failure.
- **Daemon Crash / Service Stopped:** CloudOps local hardware agent service terminated due to unhandled OS exception or auto-update reboot.
- **Firewall / Port Egress Block:** Local host firewall (Windows Defender Firewall) blocking outbound HTTP/HTTPS telemetry push to Caddy/FastAPI backend on port 8000/8443.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
text:
## 3. Immediate Diagnostic Commands
```powershell

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
section: Check Windows service status of local telemetry agent
text:
# Check Windows service status of local telemetry agent
Get-Service -Name "CloudOpsAgent*"

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
metadata.section: Check Windows service status of local telemetry agent

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
section: Verify network reachability to CloudOps Intel API
text:
# Verify network reachability to CloudOps Intel API
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 127.0.0.1 -Port 8000
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 127.0.0.1 -Port 8443

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
metadata.section: Verify network reachability to CloudOps Intel API

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
section: Check recent Windows Event Log for sudden shutdowns or power events
text:
# Check recent Windows Event Log for sudden shutdowns or power events
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=41,1074,6008} -MaxEvents 5
```

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
metadata.section: Check recent Windows Event Log for sudden shutdowns or power events

title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline
text:
## 4. Remediation Steps
1. **Restart Local Agent Service:**
   - Restart the telemetry daemon on target Lab PC:
     `Restart-Service -Name "CloudOpsAgent" -Force`
2. **Disable Aggressive Power-Saving:**
   - Configure OS power profile to high performance and disable network adapter sleep on idle:
     `powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0`
     `powercfg /change hibernate-timeout-ac 0`
3. **Validate Ingestion Key Credentials:**
   - Ensure `AGENT_INGESTION_KEY` configured in local agent matches backend configuration in `.env`.
4. **Resynchronize Sensor Inventory:**
   - Trigger a manual hardware discovery scan from Device Management dashboard to refresh hardware topology.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Lab PC & Edge Hardware Sensor Telemetry Offline

section: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
# SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

**ID:** `RUNBOOK-MEM-002`  
**Domain:** Performance & Reliability  
**Applies To:** Backend Application Nodes, Worker Pods, Python/Node/Java Runtimes  
**Severity:** Critical

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
metadata.section: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
## 1. Symptom Profile
- Monotonically increasing memory usage (RAM / Swap) over time without recovery after request completion.
- Kernel OOM Killer events logged (`dmesg` or system event log) terminating processes unexpectedly.
- Sudden container crash restarts (Exit Code 137).
- Persistent memory alerts triggered in CloudOps Intel dashboard (`memory_percent > 85%`).

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
## 2. Root Cause Classification
- **Application Cache Accumulation:** In-memory LRU caches or dictionaries growing unbounded without TTL or size eviction.
- **Unclosed Connections / File Descriptors:** Database cursor leaks, unclosed HTTP client sessions, or dangling WebSocket connections.
- **Circular References / Object Retention:** Long-lived event listeners or module-level lists retaining garbage-collected objects.
- **Buffer Bloat:** Large in-memory file buffering during telemetry batch imports or export report generations.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
## 3. Immediate Diagnostic Commands
```bash

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
section: Check memory breakdown and swap status
text:
# Check memory breakdown and swap status
free -m
vmstat 1 5

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
metadata.section: Check memory breakdown and swap status

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
# Inspect top memory-consuming processes
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 6

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
section: Check system logs for kernel OOM killer triggers
text:
# Check system logs for kernel OOM killer triggers
dmesg -T | grep -i "killed process"

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
metadata.section: Check system logs for kernel OOM killer triggers

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
# On Windows:
Get-Process | Sort-Object WorkingSet64 -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 -Property Id, ProcessName, WorkingSet64
```

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation

title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
text:
## 4. Remediation Steps
1. **Graceful Service Restart:**
   - Drain active requests and cycle the worker processes to release heap memory:
     `systemctl restart cloudops-backend` or `Restart-Service CloudOpsBackend`.
2. **Increase Swap Headroom (Temporary Buffer):**
   - Ensure swap is active to prevent immediate kernel OOM while investigating heap dumps.
3. **Inspect Application Heap Profile:**
   - Capture memory allocations using `tracemalloc` (Python) or heap snapshot tools to locate leaking data structures.
4. **Tune Worker Recycling:**
   - Configure process manager max-requests lifecycle (e.g. Uvicorn `--limit-max-requests 5000`) to periodically refresh worker memory footprint.

metadata.title: SRE Runbook: Memory Leak & Out-of-Memory (OOM) Degradation
